transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liza Morales (Redwood Product), Alex Rivera (Sentinel), Priya Singh (Sentinel), Tom Hale (Sentinel Security), Nina Gomez (PM)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough oriented toward migration. Customer currently on a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic for generative features, and evaluating consolidation to Redwood for cost and private deployment needs. They asked for parity mapping - what endpoints, parameters and behaviors map to Redwood API, how streaming/function-calls work, and how costs/latency compare.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Maya, AE on the account, Ethan will run the demo and Liza's on the product side for any console or optimize questions.
[00:00:12] Alex Rivera: Hey, thanks. quick context - we run a combo of OpenAI for chat and Anthropic on some safety-sensitive flows. looking to simplify infra and cut token costs. also Tom's here for security questions.
[00:00:25] Tom Hale: yes, main ask is auditability, kms integration, and the ability to run in our VPC eventually. SOC two is required.
[00:00:30] Ethan Park: Great, we'll focus on parity first - show how your OpenAI/Anthropic calls translate to Redwood API, and then switch to Console and Optimize to show cost/latency tooling.

-- Parity mapping / API walkthrough --
[00:01:05] Ethan Park: so high level, Redwood exposes a unified REST/SDK surface - text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking. for migration, most teams map openai chat completions -> redwood chat endpoint. e.g., messages array, role field, same stop sequences. small differences: our "model" field names follow the catalog and we expose a few model variants like rwd-gpt-3o-8k (note: placeholder), and you can pin by version.
[00:01:42] Alex Rivera: what about function calling? we rely on that heavily.
[00:01:46] Ethan Park: function calling is supported and matches openai semantics - you pass functions JSON schema and the model returns the call. edge cases: some models' arg typing varies; our Console shows a quick mapping and a test harness.
[00:02:15] Priya Singh: streaming? we need tokens as they arrive for low-latency UI.
[00:02:19] Ethan Park: yes streaming supported via SSE and websockets. we did a note - streaming chunk headers slightly different than openai sometimes, so you'll need a tiny client change but we've got examples.
[00:02:40] Alex Rivera: any differences in temperature/top_p behavior? we've seen minor distribution shifts moving between anthro and openAI.
[00:02:47] Liza Morales: model calibration matters. Optimize can run calibration evals on a sample prompt set and suggest temperature/penalty adjustments and even recommend quantization profiles to match output quality while reducing cost.

-- Console / Optimize walkthrough --
[00:03:20] Ethan Park: switching to the Console - here is per-route token breakdown, latency percentiles, and the rollout controls. you can one-click create a canary between two model variants - say rwd-3o-8k vs rwd-3o-8k-quantized.
[00:03:45] Tom Hale: can audit logs be exported to our SIEM? we need to retain logs for 1 year.
[00:03:52] Liza Morales: yes, audit logs can stream to your S3 or Splunk, and we support log retention configs on Private and Dedicated. we also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[00:04:08] Priya Singh: about Private - how does the control plane work if we want air-gapped/on-prem?
[00:04:14] Ethan Park: for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. networking is via VPC peering or private link; you manage key material if you want HSM. caveat: some enterprise features require additional ops work, we'll map that in the SOW.

-- Cost / Latency tradeoffs and serving runtime --
[00:05:10] Ethan Park: cost levers: batching, KV cache, quantization, routing to cheaper model variants. latency levers: pin to low-latency dedicated nodes, reduce batching window, or use hosted with regional routing. we'll recommend profiles based on your qps and tail latency SLOs.
[00:05:35] Alex Rivera: can we run the same model weights but quantized to int8 to cut cost? we worry about hallucination increases.
[00:05:41] Liza Morales: Optimize suggests quantization settings per workload; we usually run a small eval to see quality delta. for safety-sensitive flows we usually keep full precision or use mixed precision with eval gating.
[00:06:05] Alex Rivera: network egress costs were also a concern when using multiple clouds. can Redwood run in our region?
[00:06:10] Maya Chen: yes, we have region support and Dedicated/Private to reduce cross-cloud egress. we'll include region mapping in the parity spreadsheet.

-- Technical deep-dive / benchmarks discussion --
[00:06:50] Ethan Park: for benchmarking we recommend providing 3 representative endpoints and a set of 1000 requests across seq lengths. we'll run latency and token-cost analysis, and show per-token cost comparisons against your current bills.
[00:07:18] Priya Singh: how long does a pilot take? we need results before Q4 procurement cycles.
[00:07:23] Maya Chen: typical pilot 2-4 weeks for initial latency/cost signals; for VPC/private deployments add integration time. we can aim for a 3-week pilot starting next week if you can share samples.

-- Security/compliance specifics --
[00:08:05] Tom Hale: SOC2 yes, but also SSO/SAML and RBAC. and we need to see encryption keys access patterns.
[00:08:13] Liza Morales: SAML/SCIM provisioning supported, role-based access is configurable via Console, and key management integrates with customer KMS/HSM. we'll share our security packet and SOC2 attestation link.
[00:08:40] Tom Hale: retention of payloads - can you guarantee not to retain customer content on hosted?
[00:08:46] Maya Chen: hosted can be configured for short retention or zero-retention contracts. Dedicated and Private give you full control - zero-retention by default if required. we'll note that in the security questionnaire.

-- Electric interruptions and transcription artifacts --
[00:09:20] Speaker 6: (muffled) sorry, where did you say the KV cash is managed?
[00:09:25] Ethan Park: 
[00:09:27] Ethan Park: KV cache, yeah, sorry the transcript said KV cash - it's KV cache stored in-memory on the serving nodes, with optional shared cache across pods for prefix reuse to reduce token compute.

-- Questions from customer --
[00:10:02] Nina Gomez: what are typical unit cost savings customers see when they consolidate?
[00:10:08] Liza Morales: depends on workload; we often see 20-50% on token compute when using batching + quantization + caching. routing to cheaper variants for low-confidence responses gives more savings.
[00:10:30] Alex Rivera: any gotchas when mapping streaming or chunking behavior from anthro to redwood?
[00:10:36] Ethan Park: mainly SSE chunk envelope differences and you might need to handle partial JSON differently - we have snippet libs in the SDK to smooth that.

-- Wrap and next steps --
[00:11:05] Maya Chen: quick recap: we'll send parity mapping spreadsheet, security packet, and pricing estimate. you (Alex) will send sample requests for benchmarking, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff.
[00:11:20] Alex Rivera: sounds good. if we like the pilot numbers we'll move to a Dedicated capacity discussion.
[00:11:28] Tom Hale: please include your SOC2 and any pen-test summaries.
[00:11:33] Maya Chen: will do.
[00:11:35] Ethan Park: I'll also drop example SDK snippets for function-calling and streaming, plus a small harness to replay your workloads.
[00:11:43] Nina Gomez: ok, thanks everyone.
[00:11:46] Maya Chen: thanks all - we'll follow up with the links and schedule.
